title: customer-security-intake-alignment-matrix-and-rapid-escalation-cadence
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Create an operational alignment matrix and a lightweight, SLO-driven escalation cadence for inbound enterprise security and compliance asks (SOC2/ISO, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA, vendor questionnaires). The matrix should map request archetypes to routing lanes, required evidence bundles, SLA targets, and suggested owners. The cadence defines who to notify, how quickly to escalate based on account tier and risk signal, and which fallback policies to apply when core teams are overloaded.

Background: Enterprise customers increasingly submit structured and unstructured security requests via sales, support, and direct customer contacts. Current intake is fragmented and manually triaged, causing inconsistent SLAs and duplicated effort across Solutions Engineering, Legal, and Security. We need a lightweight decision scaffold that is operationally usable by PMs, Solutions Eng, and the Security response team, and that ties into the Console's intake UI later.

Scope (in this ticket):
- Deliver the alignment matrix (CSV + human-readable doc) that classifies request types (questionnaire, audit request, DPA clause, regional-data query, on-prem deployment controls, incident follow-up) and maps to routing lane (Fast-Path, Evidence Pool, Legal Review, On-Prem Escalation).
- Define SLA bands by account tier (self-serve, mid-market, enterprise) and by risk (low/medium/high), with explicit escalation timeouts.
- Produce an "escalation cadence" playbook: notification templates, required triage checklist, sample evidence bundles, and fallback model mapping (when to accept temporary exceptions, when to schedule remediation).
- Include suggested Console UI signals required for automated routing (account tier, hosting mode, data residency flags, questionnaire score).
- Provide an initial rollout plan with owners, monitoring metrics, and post-rollout evaluation criteria.

Out of scope: building the intake UI or automation; that will be a follow-up ENG project.

Acceptance criteria:
- Alignment matrix CSV with columns: request_type, example_signals, suggested_lane, sla_hours_by_tier, required_documents, default_owner_role, followup_steps.
- Playbook doc with step-by-step cadence for Fast-Path requests (<=24h for enterprise P1), Evidence Pool handling (48-96h typical), and Legal Review triggers.
- Stakeholder sign-off from Security, Legal, Support, and Sales (email threads or Confluence approval).
- Monitoring plan: dashboards to track median time to first-touch, percent of requests resolved within SLA by lane, and false-positive routing rate.

Success metrics (first 60 days post-rollout):
- Median first-touch time reduced from current baseline by 50% for enterprise lanes.
- >= 85% of Fast-Path items meet SLA.
- Reduction in cross-team assignment churn by 30%.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Tight SLAs may require more engineering automation; initial playbook accepts some manual triage for low-volume lanes.
- Conservative default routing to Legal increases cycle time; matrix must clearly define evidence thresholds to avoid over-routing.

Rollout plan:
1) Draft matrix + playbook (this ticket) -> deliverables linked below.
2) 2-week review with Security/Legal/Support -> incorporate feedback.
3) Train triage leads (Solutions Eng rotas) and run a 2-week pilot with new routing rules for inbound requests.
4) Collect metrics and iterate; create follow-up ENG ticket to wire signals into Console intake UI for automation.

Owner: PM (Aisha) + rotating Triage Lead (Liam).
